transcript.text: Every time I put the oven on it runs for a few minutes and then the trip switch goes and half the house loses power. Reset it 3 times tonight. Hotpoint built-in, about 9 years old. What could cause this?

The most likely cause is a failing oven heating element, especially since it runs for a few minutes before tripping. As an element heats up, its insulation can break down and leak a small amount of current to earth. The RCD/RCBO then trips to protect against electric shock. This is common on ovens of that age.

Other possible causes include:

• Fan oven element, grill element, or lower/base element failing (depending on which cooking mode is selected)
• A damaged or heat-affected internal wire/terminal
• A faulty fan motor, thermostat, selector switch, or oven light circuit
• Moisture/grease contamination causing leakage
• Less commonly, a fault in the cooker supply cable, connection unit, or consumer-unit circuit

“Half the house” losing power suggests it is probably an RCD protecting several circuits, rather than just the oven’s individual breaker. If the switch that trips has a Test button, it is likely an RCD/RCBO. It is doing its job — don’t keep resetting it and trying the oven, particularly after three trips.

What to do now:

1. Stop using the oven until it is checked.
2. Turn it off at the cooker isolation switch if you have one (usually a red switch nearby), and leave it off.
3. Arrange for a qualified appliance repair engineer or electrician to test it. They can insulation-test the elements and wiring and usually identify the culprit quickly.
4. Do not fit a larger breaker, bypass the RCD, or attempt internal repairs unless you are qualified.

If there is any burning smell, smoke, crackling, heat around the cooker switch, or visible damage, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit if safe to do so and seek urgent electrical help.
